paragraphs.text: Jesus ✠ Christ. An encomium by our holy father, honored in every way, Apa Stephen, bishop of the city of Hnes, which he delivered on the feast of the holy martyr of Christ Jesus, Apa Elias, which is the twenty-first of Phamenoth, when they were celebrating his feast in his shrine. In peace. Amen.
There are trees growing in distant lands. Even though we have never seen them face to face, we come to know their beauty and their sweetness by enjoying their fruits.
The prize-winning martyrs who arose city by city and region by region are like this. Even though we did not go
with them to the tribunal, and did not watch the contest they endured for Christ,
we come to know their greatness and their honor with the Lord through the abundance of the gifts of grace present in their shrines.
Such a one, truly, is our chosen crown-bearer, the exalted prize-winner, holy Elias, who is the reason for your gathering today, O pious ones.
O prize-bearer Elias, you are light both in name and in virtue!
I see the holy saying of our Savior fulfilled in you: "Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father."
Christ, however, said this about all the righteous.
But holy Elias came to resemble the sun in his name, in his virtue and in his light, through the very name he was given.
For in Greek, Elias means "the sun."
First the name comes, together with birth, that is, birth in the flesh.
Afterward his way of life appeared and confirmed the name.
As the name of this saint is, then, so is the honor of his praise, as it is written in the Psalms.
Yet the visible sun's light has an end,
but the light of the martyrs is imperishable.
The sun sets, and then it rises again.
The prize-winning martyrs set in the body when they die,
but they come with the Lord in glory, and the crown for their sufferings is prepared for them.
But let us come to the subject of your gathering for today's commemoration of holy Elias, who steered his soldiering well, like a skilled charioteer.
Elias is the true general of Christ the King, and the physician of all who are sick.
He was not a laborer who works the land, nor
did he eat his bread by the sweat of his face,
nor did he live in poverty, so that you could not say that the hardship of poverty forced him to run into this stadium of martyrdom.
No, he was a nobleman among those of high rank.
He was rich among the prominent.
He was rich [?] in the gifts of Christ.
He was a mighty warrior against the visible enemies,
and even more a conqueror of the evil adversaries who are hidden.
He was close to the king of this world,
and he is a friend of the King of heaven and earth, Christ Jesus.
He was enrolled for military service in an earthly regiment;
he was also enrolled in the heavenly fold [?] through the contest of confession.
Once he was a physician in a single city,
but now he has become a healer of those near him and those far away.
How fine is the stadium of your martyrdom, O truly noble one!
Your crown never fades.
The fruits of your righteousness are beyond counting.
To whom among the saints shall I compare you, O holy Elias?
I will compare you to the one who bears the same name as you, Elijah,
who was taken up by whirlwinds and chariots of fire,
who shut heaven and opened it again by the word of his mouth.
For that Elijah is the one who fasted forty days and forty nights.
O this great wonder-worker! After he had burned up two captains of fifty together with their hundred soldiers,
and after he had slaughtered the four hundred and fifty priests of Baal,
in the end he fled before the threat of a harlot woman.
But you, O bearer of victory, bearer of prizes, bearer of God, bearer of the Spirit and bearer of the crown of the New Covenant,
honored martyr,
faithful noble one,
unconquerable athlete,
victorious contender,
holy Elias: you stood firm before the threats of kings, and you were not ashamed before the faces of the potentates.
You trampled on the power of the fire.
You were strong in the war against your enemies.
I will compare you with the wise Daniel, who is truly your equal in both service and virtue.
He stood before the kings of the Chaldeans;
and you too, O honored athlete, stood before those who shared one inheritance with them.
He despised the decrees of Darius and Cyrus;
you too, O crown-bearer of Christ, despised the idol-worshippers.
Daniel was thrown into the lions' den because he did not obey the decree of the Persians and the Medes;
but you, O righteous one, endured for the confession of Christ not only the ordeal of the wild beasts,
but you stood strong through many contests.
I compare you with the learned physician, the beloved Luke the evangelist.
You came to resemble him by following Christ and by becoming a martyr for him.
How, then, shall I portray for you the story of holy Elias? Shall it be the grace that came to him from the Lord,
or shall I tell of his struggle for God?
Or rather of the help of the Most High, which helped you?
Shall I tell of the wrath and madness of the tyrant, or of the endurance of this holy martyr?
He was like a sheep among wolves;
he was like a lily among thorns.
He was a giver of light among those in the darkness of the error of idols, and those people lived in luxury,
but this noble one was kept in check by God.
They worshipped the things their own hands had made; but holy Elias worshipped the Creator alone, who is God.
And the world-ruler of darkness urged him toward darkness as well.
But the noble martyr's citizenship was in heaven.
Picture, then, at last, the splendid theater full of grace:
a single man, not yet a saint, standing between God
and men, between angels and demons.
The earthly were forcing him to sacrifice to earthly gods;
but the heavenly King, Christ, was strengthening his noble one for the contest.
"Will you sacrifice, then, Elias, or not?" he said.
The holy martyr said, "I am a physician who heals others.
How then could I bear to let my own soul fall sick with idolatry?
I am a soldier in the army that belongs to the earth, but I do not wish to be cut off from the armies of the angels.
I am a citizen of the city on earth, but from this day on I will choose for myself the heavenly Jerusalem, the truly existing city of the Holy One."
What, then, will the powers of darkness do now?
What will the God-fighting king do?
He flattered.
He threatened.
He pleaded.
He raged.
And, to put it briefly:
the torrents came down,
the rains came, and there blew
the winds.
They beat against the mind of this saint, and could not move him, for he was built on the immovable rock, Christ.
Finally, when the first round of training had been completed,
they called the athlete and champion of the truth into the contest.
Again, sufferings exceedingly great.
Again, many confiscations and punishments.
Again, the madness of the executioners.
Again, from strength to strength,
from one kingdom to another people,
from tribunal to tribunal,
from harsh sufferings to many afflictions.
For the weapons of his soldiering were not of the flesh, but were the powers of God.
He showed himself to be following Christ, who stood before the high priests, Herod and Pilate.
For the wise say of the nature of gold that what is tested in the furnace a first, a second and a third time is genuine gold.
So also the holy martyr, holy Elias, having proved himself in the first trial, the second and the third,
for this reason his crown became brilliant in heaven and on earth.
He passed through fire and water, but the place of refreshment is laid up for him above, as the psalmist says.
They hung him on wood, but it was so that he might be like his Teacher, who was crucified for us.
He renounced his kinsfolk, who were not of his mind, and destructive pleasure,
but the banquet of the kingdom of heaven is prepared for him.
He left behind him the ranks of this passing age, but endless good things are his.
He turned his face away from the kings of the earth,
but he gazed upon the vision of the light of the holy, consubstantial Trinity.
They took off his head with the sword, but he went to his true Head, Christ. He renounced the king's belt, but became like David, who cast Saul's armor off himself.
Women came out before that man, dancing over his victory over the Philistine.
But as for this noble one, angels are his judges of the games, proclaiming that he has conquered the father of all the foreigners, that is, the devil.
You are blessed now, O prize-bearer, and your crown is brilliant.
How fine is your victory, which passed through many contests for the love of God!
And the Lord will crown you with the crown of righteousness.
Let no one now be unbelieving on hearing of all the sufferings that this prize-winning martyr endured for Christ.
For great is the abundance of healings that take place every day in his shrine;
they spread out over everyone, almost like the rays of the shining sun.
What, then, are the healing of the sick,
the casting out of demons,
and those who had come near the gates of death, whom he restores to life again through the intercessions he makes for us before the Lord Jesus?
For he knows how to treat those with dropsy by the art of his medicine, without payment;
he knows how to heal the sick, taking away what pains [?] their limbs.
In short, this holy one heals everyone, receiving grace from God and giving each person what he asks of him,
fulfilling the request of each one who comes to his holy shrine.
You see what a patron we have, fighting for us against the hidden enemies,
and acting as healer of our bodies as well.
Indeed, even the day of his departure fits the subject in hand [?].
For wise physicians used to say about this month, Phamenoth, that it is by nature a month that brings sickness,
since it is then that the trees put forth their shoots.
For it was at that time that God went down to Egypt to bring the children of Israel out from its midst with signs and wonders.
Also in this month day and night come into balance [?], becoming equal to each other.
That is why grace rightly arranged for the feast of this wise physician to fall in the month that brings sickness,
so that his holy prayers might save everyone who is sick in soul and body.
These things I have set before your love concerning the contest of this noble martyr, holy Elias.
Now, my beloved, I wish to say a word of praise about the holy brothers whose bones have been laid in his shrine.
"How good, how pleasant it is for brothers to dwell in one place," in the words of David the hymn-writer.
And the wise Solomon also said, "There are three that walk well."
That is why the Lord rightly arranged for the bones of these three saints to be laid beside one another,
so that the holy Trinity, for which they contended, might be glorified when these three holy ones are named.
You, then, O pious people, children of grace, who wish to run well and gain the kingdom of Christ: it is good to make haste to come to this place today, and every day as well.
But let no one seek only the healing of his body and neglect the sins of our souls.

Look at the sufferings the martyrs endured: shut up in prisons, lying on the ground with their blood flowing on the earth, hungry and thirsty, their bodies covered with wounds, because they would not give in, all the while beseeching God night and day.
O what a great shame that we sleep, our hearts slack, not caring about the sufferings the saints endured until they were found worthy of life!

Above all, the Lord of the saints, Jesus, kept watch night after night in prayer, not for his own sake, God forbid, but for ours, wretched as we are, to teach us the way to escape the snares of the evil one.
See that everything in this world is vain.
What profit is it to us to celebrate the feasts of the martyrs, who contended against sin unto death for the faith of the Son of God,
while we ourselves are full of every kind of passion and many kinds of sin, and have not repented before the messenger comes seeking us?
In a little while the reaper will come face to face and test [?] to see what kind it is,
in case he should find no flour inside it, that is, deeds full of every virtue, but only the outward form of a husk, that is, hypocrisy.
For the name we bear and the rank we hold are one thing, and the deeds we do in secret are another,
as it is written: "What they do in secret is shameful even to speak of."
Woe to the man whom Satan blinds and in whom he dwells through the desire for defilement, because he did not give it up while he was alive!
And if he dies before repenting, he will be in the place of eternity and will find no one to look after him [?].
For I have said that there are disciples of his whom he would send out to preach [?].
The evangelist Luke said: "He gave them authority to cast out unclean spirits and to heal every disease and every sickness."
The good thing is that he heals a person's soul and body of the unclean spirits, that is, defiled thoughts [?].
O man, cast out of your soul these passions, which harm us more than anything, and you will escape the sleepless worm in Amente.
Drive away from you the desire of the flesh, which is against the Spirit, and you will not be cast out of the heavenly dwelling places.
Let our honoring of the martyrs not consist only in coming into their shrines;
let us rather imitate their courage, let us hold fast to
their endurance,
let us emulate their love for God. They
conquered the world and its desires of every kind; let us
also not let the world and its will conquer us. They
despised the threats of tortures; let us also not be conquered by the deceit of the devil.
They won for themselves the friendship of heaven;
let us also lay up our citizenship in that place.
For this is the way we shall become friends and kin of the saints.
And if we are not engaged in martyrdom as holy Elias was, then
let us live in righteousness like the brothers who lie beside him.
This too is the wisdom of God: he arranged for the bones of the ascetics to lie beside those of the martyr, so that their example might become an encouragement to everyone toward repentance.
So, if you live in a time of persecution, here is the one who conquered in the persecutions, holy Elias. Again,
if you live without persecution, here are those who proved genuine in their way of life and their asceticism. For
the ascetic life is of equal weight [?], not inferior to martyrdom. But
to show that this is so, I will bring you the wise apostle as advocate in this case,
when he recounted to us the faith of each of the saints.
When he came to Gideon, Barak, Samson, David and Samuel, after listing those who conquered in the stadium of martyrdom, he joined the monastic life to them, speaking thus:
"They wandered in deserts and mountains and caves and holes in the ground, in want, afflicted, ill-treated, of whom the world was not worthy."
At the end he crowned them all with the name of martyrdom, saying, "Therefore, since we have this great multitude of witnesses set before us, let us run with endurance the contest set before us."
You see that the monastic life is the sister of martyrdom, for whoever practices it without hypocrisy and falsehood.
For Christ himself set forth for us the pattern of these two contests in his own person.
He conquered the devil when he withdrew into the desert.
And again he established the salvation of the whole world through the victory of the cross. To those in the desert
he gave victory by becoming their leader in this. Again,
for those who ran their course in the stadium of martyrdom, he became their crown.
And we too, my brothers, let us follow the Lord and the things of the Lord. Let us confess
the Lord and the holy martyrs.
Let us be holy for him like those who purified themselves for him through asceticism. Let us keep watch
over our faith like the holy martyrs.
Let us be sharers in the love of the Spirit.
For even if we cannot shine like the sun, let us at least be seen in the rank of the stars.
This is what I mean: even if we cannot attain the greatness of the martyrs' contests,
let us at least be found in the ranks of the faithful. Even
if we cannot love God as he loved us, let us at least love one another in the same way.
And even if you have nothing to give your neighbor, comfort him with your words; strengthen him with the promise of the kingdom of heaven.
Tell him the saying of the apostle: "The sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory that will be revealed to us."
For poverty is a martyrdom for the one who bears it with thanksgiving.
For this is how Christ, the life of us all, put it: "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven."
And those who have been persecuted for righteousness' sake are the ones who will be called sons of God; these are the martyrs.
And we, my beloved, let us love our neighbors as the martyrs loved God when they poured out their blood for him, so that we may find mercy on the day when we shall stand before him.
May the Lord bless you all, from the least of you to the greatest, and rouse you from this negligence.
Be sober and watchful, for the adversary, the devil, walks in darkness night and day without our seeing him, seeking to devour our souls. I beseech
you all that each of you examine his life, whether he has done well or falls short. If
he has sinned, let him repent of what he has done, and I trust in God and in the prayers of the holy martyr, holy Elias, that he will forgive him.
Let us not linger, putting things off from day to day, lest the messenger of death overtake us and find us unprepared, not having repented, and we curse the day we were born, in vain.
For when the hour has passed from us, [?] the door; whoever is found inside, whether good or bad, has passed on.
It has passed. It is good for us to repent before the door of repentance is shut on us.
May our God, Christ Jesus, the Lord of heaven and earth, set his peace upon us and drive the devil and his demons far from us.
To him be glory, honor and worship, with his good Father and the Holy Spirit, the perfect Trinity in unity and unity in consubstantial Trinity, forever and ever. Amen.

Jesus ✠ Christ. This is the martyrdom of the holy martyr of Christ, Apa Elias, who completed his glorious contest, together with those who were with him, on the fifteenth of Paremhotep, in peace. Amen.

It came to pass, when the apostles had completed their preaching according to the command of our Savior Jesus, that they brought the church to its fullness from the rising of the sun to its setting, so that the sweet fragrance of its offering spread up to the heavens, and their hearts, moreover, were upright toward the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ.
And the name of God was glorified, and Mastema was put to shame.
The glory of the church was revealed, and the idols ceased, until two hundred and eighty-six years had passed since the ascension of our Savior Jesus Christ the Lord.
The whole world was of one faith, worshipping one God, Jesus Christ, with his good Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever and ever. Amen. It came to pass,
after this, when a long time had gone by, that the world sinned through idolatry.
And when Mastema realized that he had been put to shame together with those who were his,
he took counsel with those who were his, saying, "What shall we do? Perhaps the world will turn to me again and listen to me." He thought up
crafty schemes of this kind, so that he might make the world turn aside as before. In the same way, it was necessary that the martyrs receive crowns.

He took counsel in his heart, saying, "I will enter the hearts of the great kings who rule the world and turn their hearts, and make them abandon the God of heaven, worship idols, and shed blood, and do other confused deeds that profit nothing."

These are the names of the kings who ruled at that time, each in his own region: Aliberianus, who was king of Konoia [?]; Nicomedes, who was king of Persia; Eutychodorus, who was king of Media; Diocletian, who was king of the Romans; Herodianus, who was king of Thentike [?].
When the devil had led them astray, they abandoned the God of heaven, worshipped idols, and shed the blood of all the Christians, each in his own region.
Now there was a man named Soterichus, who was Caesar under Herodianus, the king of Thentike [?].

When he saw that they were abusing all the Christians for the sake of the holy name of our Lord Jesus Christ, and moreover saw great wonders worked through them, he too renounced the idols and believed in the true God, Jesus Christ.
And the holy Soterichus began to oppose the king.
Using his authority, he sent and released all the Christians who were in prison.
When King Herodianus heard of it, he was very angry; he sent in haste and had Soterichus brought to him.

When he came, the king said to him, "Soterichus, what is this audacity you have committed in my kingdom? You have opposed my decree concerning the worship of the gods, although there is no one after me but you in my kingdom."
Soterichus answered, "From now on I will never again submit to a king of this world; I will cling to the feet of the true King, Christ Jesus, whose kingdom has no end and will never be dissolved.
Now then, O king, do not trouble me. I will not worship your abominable gods, nor will I abandon my King Jesus."
When he had said these things, the king was very angry and ordered him to be bound.
When his soldiers saw him bound, they cried out, "Our lord, give the order and we will set you free and save you from the king."
He said to them, "No, since it is the will of my Lord Jesus that I die for his holy name.
Our Lord Jesus does not want war, but peace.
What I ask of you is this: that you [?] with all your hearts and die for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that you may be enrolled in the army of the angels."
They all cried out, "What you have said, we are ready to do with joy."
Standing by him that day were five tribunes with their host of soldiers.
They came to the king with one mind, saying, "We are all Christians. The death by which our lord Soterichus is to die, by that same death we too will die."
When the king heard them he was very angry; indeed, he was shaken.
He ordered them to be put into ships and taken out to the open sea. They cut off their heads and threw their bodies into the sea, while the holy Soterichus stood over them praying.
He looked and saw their souls like white doves going up to heaven.
Then he too stretched out his head, and they cut it off. This is how the holy Soterichus completed his martyrdom, with his whole household and the soldiers who stood by him.
Their total number was four hundred and fifty-six, together with the five tribunes, and they were all perfected on a single day, the ninth of Tobe, in peace. Amen.
Listen now, my brothers, and I will tell you that God does not forget those who trust in him, but helps them and gives them strength.
It came to pass, after the holy Soterichus had been martyred, that there was
a soldier in the palace, thirty-three years old, whose name was Elias. He was handsome of face, mighty in strength, and perfect in every good work.
He was a physician and stood before the king at all times because of the healings he performed. Indeed, whenever the king or his nobles fell ill, it was he who treated them.
For this reason everyone in the palace loved him, from the least to the greatest.
Now the holy Elias thought daily about the holy Soterichus,
and he would pray, saying, "When I am found worthy, reveal yourself to me, that I may see your face again.
As the Lord lives, and as your soul lives, the death by which you died, I too will die by it."
As he lay thinking about these things, a voice came to him: "Elias, Elias."
He said, "Here I am, lord. Who are you that call me?"
The holy Elias thought that the king had fallen ill and had sent for him to heal him.
The voice came to him a second time: "My chosen Elias, I am not a king, as you think, who needs a physician to heal him. Open your eyes and know who I am. I am
Jesus, the fragrance of the incense of the Father. I am Jesus, the true physician, who heals every sickness and cures those who suffer.
I am Jesus, the fragrance of the true vine of the good Father.
I am Jesus, the gladness of the water of the Acherusian Lake.
I am Jesus, the bond of the ages that cannot be undone.
I am Jesus, who helps everyone who believes in him with all their heart."
When the holy Elias heard these things, he lifted his eyes and saw him mounted on the chariots of the cherubim,
with Michael the archangel at his right and the holy Soterichus at his left, clothed in a glorious garment such as no king of this world could wear.

When the holy Elias saw these things, he prostrated himself before the Lord, saying, "Forgive me, my Lord, for I am a sinful man. But I know, my Lord, that you grant repentance to the sinner if he turns back and repents.
So I beseech you, my Lord Jesus Christ, who forgives all sinners: forgive me too all the sins I committed when I did not know you."
At that very hour he raised him up, saying to him, "Arise, my chosen Elias. I am
Jesus, who helps you. Truly I tell you, I will grant you my kingdom; for behold, I have already written your name in the book of life.

For I know that you will suffer many afflictions for my name. But do not be afraid: they will not prevail against you, for I am with you in every place they take you, giving you strength until you complete your contest.
When the king sends for you tomorrow, do not go to him as you usually do. He will send for you a second time, and they will compel you until they bring you to him.
He will ask you, 'Why did you not come to me quickly when I sent for you?' Answer
him without any fear, with the holy words that I will put into your mouth.
I am with you, and I will fill you with the Holy Spirit, giving you strength until my name is glorified through you.
Arise now, come and greet your companion Soterichus, whom you asked to see."
When the Savior had said this to him, he gave him peace and went up to heaven in glory, while the holy Elias gazed after him.
Likewise a great fragrance spread out from the bedchamber in which the holy Elias was lying. In the morning,
when the holy Elias had not gone to the king's palace as he usually did,
the king sent for him. The messengers said to him, "The king summons you, Elias.
Why have you not come to the palace today?"
The saint said to them, "Go and tell the king: Thus says Elias, the servant of Jesus Christ: From this moment on I will not submit to you, for it is not fitting for the living to
submit to the dead; rather, the dead submits to the living, so that he too may live through him."
When the messengers had heard these things from the holy Elias, they reported them to the king just as he had spoken.
When the king heard these things he was very angry, and he sent a general after him to bring him by force.
When they had brought him, the king saw that his face was full of great glory.
The king said to him, "Elias, I loved you dearly. Why have you become so very arrogant and despised me? You did not come to me when I sent for you; instead you likened me to a dead man."

The holy Elias said to him, "All the gods of the nations are silver and gold, the work of human hands. They have eyes and do not see; they have ears and do not hear; they have hands and cannot touch; they have feet and do not walk. Those who made them are like them, and so is everyone who worships them.
So you see, O king, that you are a dead man, since you worship dead gods.
My God, Jesus Christ, is a living God, and everyone who is alive and believes in him will live through him. It is written
thus: 'As my Father lives, so I too live because of my Father; and you also will live because of me.'"
When the king heard these things he said, "Elias, listen to me and worship my gods, so that you may be spared great and cruel tortures.
Do you want to die the shameful death of Soterichus?"
The saint said to him, "O king, the death of Soterichus is not a shameful death; on the contrary, it is most honorable,
for it is written thus: 'Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his holy ones.'"
The king said to him, "Elias, my beloved, do not make me come to hate you [?]."
But the holy Elias resolved to put the king's gods to shame.
He said, "O king, since you have pressed me so hard, I for my part do not wish to grieve you.
But I want you to let no one enter the temple until I have offered sacrifice to your gods."
So the king ordered that the holy Elias be allowed to go in.
Then the saint took an axe with him under his clothes.

When he saw the idols standing on their pedestals, he set upon them with the great power of God and threw them down from their pedestals with the axe in his hand, and he cut their heads off their bodies.
The angel of the Lord hung their bodies up in the air in the middle of the temple,
while their heads lay at the feet of their pedestals.
Then the holy Elias came outside and said to the king, "O king, tell me about your gods,
for I went into the temple and did not find the gods there to worship them —
since it is written in the Gospel, 'The Lord your God is the one you shall worship, and him alone shall you serve.'"
When the king heard this he got up quickly and went into the temple, but he saw nothing except heads lying at the feet of their pedestals.
He ordered the priests brought to him and asked them, "Where are the gods we worship?"
They were afraid and could not think what to say; worse, they tried to deceive the king.
They said to the king, "O our lord the king, live forever! The gods fled from us, saying, 'Enemies of the king mean to rise up against him; we will go and fight the war and then return to you.'"
When the holy Elias heard this, he rejoiced greatly and laughed: "So then your gods forgot to take their heads with them when they went off to war!"
When the king heard this he was deeply ashamed, and indeed very angry with the priests.
He said, "You who deserve to be put to the sword! Do gods go to war without heads on them?"

While the king was saying this, behold, a voice came out of the bodies of the idols hanging in the air in the temple, saying, "O King Herodianus, do not believe these priests who are deceiving you, saying that we have gone to war to save you.
We are not gods; we have no power to wage war.
For behold, we are hanging in midair by the God of the holy Elias, and we have not been able to save ourselves. How then could we save you?
We beg you, O king, to ask the holy Elias to let us down, lest we fall."
The king turned to the holy Elias and said to him, "Elias, I know that nothing is impossible for you. When you were in the palace you used to heal every sickness without trouble.
So I ask you now to heal the gods, not to leave them hanging, and to join their heads to their bodies again."
The holy Elias said to the king, "Do men heal gods, or do gods heal men?"
The king said to him, "Truly, God heals man."
The holy Elias said, "Truly you have judged rightly, O king.
Why then do you press me to heal these gods of yours, calling them gods?
If they are gods, let them heal themselves.
But since you have asked me, O king, to let them down so that they stop hanging there, I will not grieve you."
And the holy Elias lifted his eyes to heaven and prayed,
saying, "Hear me, Jesus, the ear that hears, the eye that sees. I beseech you to make these idols fall to the ground and be [?], so that their memory may be wiped from the earth."
At once the idols fell to the ground and shattered and became like dust, together with their heads lying on the ground.
After that a strong wind blew and swept away the dust of the idols, and they vanished from the earth.
When the king saw what had happened, he said to the saint, "O Elias, is this the thanks you have shown me? I showed you favor, and you have made my gods like dust before the wind."
The saint said to the king, "It is written that the ungodly are like the dust that the wind drives from the face of the earth.
And you too, O king, if you remain ungodly, will go to destruction like them."
When the king heard this he was very angry,
and he ordered him to be locked up until the next day.
The holy Elias spent the whole night praying to God.
As for the king, while he lay asleep that night, behold, the devil came in to him in the form of a great black dragon, whose [?] was very terrifying.
When the king saw him he was alarmed and cried out, "Who are you, whom I see in this form and this terrifying shape?"
The dragon answered, "I am the devil, the enemy of the Christians.

Why have you let Elias go, this Christian sorcerer who destroyed your gods? Do you want to become a Christian yourself and make yourself my enemy? If so, I will punish you with great vengeance — for look, you see how terrible I am."
The king was greatly alarmed; the dragon's eyes were blazing with fire.
The king said to him, "My lord, whatever you tell me, I will do; only do not destroy me." The devil said
to him, "If you will listen to me, when you rise early tomorrow, have gods of gold made for you in place of the stone ones that Elias destroyed.
And force him to worship them. If he disobeys you, torture him all the more."
When the dragon had said these things, he led the king's heart astray, turned into a flame of fire, and flew away.
When the king rose early, he ordered gods of gold to be made for him in place of the stone ones, just as the devil had said.
And he had the holy Elias brought to him.

The king said to him, "What will you say to me now? Can you say that these are not gods? Look, I have made them of gold. Now listen to me: come and worship them before I torture you, for I will not spare you a single day more."
The holy Elias said to the king, "Whatever you want, do it to me quickly,
for I will not abandon my Lord Jesus Christ to worship things made by human hands."
When the king heard this he was very angry, and he ordered that his feet be broken with swords and their bones drawn out.
The king said to him, "Elias, you have seen the beginning of the tortures, how very cruel they are. Listen to me now and escape this cruel torment."
The saint said to him, "I care nothing for your tortures, you son of the devil."
When the king heard this he was very angry, and he ordered his nails to be pulled out one by one, those of his hands and those of his feet.
The king said to him, "Listen to me, so that you may escape cruel tortures: sacrifice, and I will let you go."
The holy Elias said, "What you have done to me now is a good thing, O king,
for it is written thus: 'Where, O death, is your sting?' And the sting of death is sin. So this sting of death is what you have pulled out of me."
When the king realized that he felt no pain under this torture,
he ordered them to strip the skin from his ribs and draw out his sinews one by one.
These were the tortures they inflicted on him that day.
The king said, "O Elias, there is still another torture I will give you. If you do not sacrifice, I swear by the welfare of my kingdom, I will kill you with an evil death."
The holy Elias said to him, "It is written: 'Do not fear those who will kill your body; they have no power to destroy your soul.'"
When the king heard these things, he ordered him to be placed on an iron bed and a fire to be lit under him for three hours, the fire blazing beneath him.
They were pouring [?] over his body, but he did not feel this harsh torture; instead
he was reciting this psalm, saying: "The saints will boast in glory and honor; they will rejoice upon their beds. The praises of God are in their throats, and two-edged swords in their hands."
When the king saw that he did not feel these tortures,
he rose at once from the tribunal and went down to the sea.
He had the holy Elias brought to him, along with two other very fierce beasts, a [?]

and a lioness with young. The king ordered a small boat to be brought to him [?], and he had all its tackle removed. He had the holy Elias put aboard it with the other beasts, and had it towed out into the middle of the open sea, tied behind the [?]. Then they cut the boat's ropes and left it drifting in the middle of the sea, with the holy Elias aboard it along with the other beasts.
He turned his face toward the east and prayed, saying: "I beseech you, Jesus, Son of the living God, who saved Daniel and shut the mouths of the lions:
save me too from these wild beasts.
You are the one who saved Jonah the prophet when he was in the belly of the sea monster:
save me too in the midst of this raging sea."
While the holy Elias was still praying, he saw that the beasts too had turned their faces toward the east and were crying out to God in their own tongue.

The righteous man turned again and prayed, saying: "You who guided Joseph, guide me too, together with these two dumb animals, in the midst of these waters; for just as they have cast me adrift, they have cast these adrift as well. And behold, they glorify your holy name."
At that very hour Michael and Gabriel came down from heaven. They went to him, greeted him and said to him, "Be strong, holy Elias; no one will be able to harm you.
For we have been sent to you to steer your boat until we bring you to the land of Kounthia, because a great contest awaits you there."
While the angels were speaking with him, one sat at the bow of the boat
and the other at its stern, and at once they came to the borders of Kounthia.
Then the angels of the Lord greeted him and went up to heaven in glory, in the peace of God. Amen.
This is the first martyrdom of Saint Elias, which he underwent under Hierodianus, king of Thendike [?]. In peace. [?]
Now Liberianus, king of Kounthia, came out to the sea. He looked out over it and saw the little boat floating on the sea,
with Saint Elias aboard it and the beasts licking his feet. At once the king ordered
that he be brought into the city.
He saw Saint Elias with his face beaming with joy, and the king said to him, "What country are you from? Where do you come from?"
The saint said to him, "I am a man of Thentike [?], and I belong to Christ."
When King Liberianus heard the name of Jesus, he grew very angry, for he himself was an idol-worshipper.
He said, "Truly you are one of those Christian magicians.
Well then, the signs of your magic are plain to see: if you were not a magician, you would not have been saved from these fierce beasts.
But I am the one who will torture you, to match your magic."

The devil had put a scheme into his heart to do great evils to the saint. The king ordered him to be bound with iron chains and thrown into a bronze dungeon until the next day, when he would give him a hearing.
He had the beasts taken to the beast arena.
Early the next morning the king ordered the holy Elias to be brought to him in the city theater, so that he could hear him in public.
When the king [saw] him, he first asked him, "What is your name?" The saint said to him, "My name according to the world is Elias; but in the Spirit it is the name given me by Jesus Christ."
The king said to him, "So you have two names, unlike everyone else?"
The saint said to him, "I am not the only one with two names: everyone who believes in my God has their strength changed

and receives a name according to the Spirit. For what is born of the flesh is flesh, and what is born of the Spirit is spirit. So there is one name according to the flesh and another according to the Spirit."
When the king heard this, he said, "Elias, these words will do you no good; rather, you will die a cruel death,
and no one will be able to save you from my hands."
Saint Elias said to him, "I would rather die at your hands
than disobey Jesus my God."
When the king heard these things,

he ordered his sides to be scraped with iron claws and knives, down to his feet. While they were scraping him, the king called out to him, "Listen to me and sacrifice, so that you may be saved from great torments."
But the saint said nothing at all; he only gazed up to heaven.
When the king saw that he felt nothing, he ordered him thrown into a pit full of boiling oil and a fire lit beneath it for two hours,
so that his body was badly burned. After that they poured sulfur and pitch over him,
and their flame rose forty cubits above his body.
The king thought he was already dead.
So he cried out, "O Elias, where is Jesus your God now? Let him save you from my hands."

But the saint, filled with the Holy Spirit, there in the fire, cried out, "Shut your mouth and be silent, lawless king, speaking the name of my God with your defiled mouth!" When the king heard that he was not dead, he was utterly astonished
and struck his hands together.
He said, "Truly I know that you will get the better of me until I undo your magic. I will send for a magician greater than you, who will undo your sorceries,

and I will teach you a lesson." He had him thrown into a cell and hung up by the feet, with his head lowered into a jar full of vinegar and lye [?], the lye reaching up to his chest. He sealed the door with his ring until he could send for the magician and have him tested against him.
When the king had gone out of the place where the holy Elias was shut in,
behold, Michael the archangel came to the holy Elias. He took him down from where he hung, sealed his body with the sign, and made it as if nothing had touched it at all.
He also brought him some fruit from the trees of paradise to eat.
For he had not eaten since the day they put him on the sea with the beasts.
Michael said to him, "Be strong, O holy Elias, victorious warrior, crown-winning champion, fellow heir of Jesus Christ.
Truly I tell you, they have already prepared your
throne in the seventh heaven, at the right hand of Christ. Do not be afraid: I will stand by you, helping you in every place they take you."
When the angel of the Lord had said these things to him, he went up to heaven in glory.
Then the king sent for a great master magician named Theocletus, who was famous throughout the land of Kounthia. When he came to him,
the king said to him, "Theocletus, I have heard of your fame as a master magician.
Now then, let your mastery be shown on this Christian.
For I have heard that they have a god called Jesus, and whenever they invoke his name, he helps them in every need."
When Theocletus the magician heard this, he laughed and said to the king, "Do not let these things trouble you. I will show you that I have the power to undo the magic of the Christians."
The magician rose and went with the king outside the palace,
and they went into a tomb.
He turned his face toward the west
and invoked the Tartarouchos, saying, "Send me up a soul to tell the king that I am able to undo the magic of the Christians."
At once the Tartarouchos came up with a multitude of souls in chains, tormenting them. The magician asked the Tartarouchos to open the mouth of a soul so that it might speak.

When the soul was given leave to speak, it cried out, "Woe to you, King Liberianus! Woe to everyone who denies this name, Jesus! And you, Theocletus the magician, you do not have the power to fight against Elias the Christian.

But blessed are you, for you will be saved through him, and you will receive what your name means: 'the one whom God saved.' You will try to do evil to Elias, but he will do good to you; you will try to kill him, but he will give you life. Yet I adjure you by the grace that is about to come upon you: when you receive life through the holy Elias, remember me too.
Perhaps he will entreat his God Jesus to rescue us [?] from the punishments we are in. For we are tormented all the more because we denied him in our ignorance while we were in the world.
Now I know that Jesus is a merciful God, who forgives the sins of all who turn to him with an upright heart."

When the king heard these words, he said, "What shall we do with Elias the Christian, who has made the demons appear in a phantasm and speak these lies, so that we would be afraid and spare him?" The magician answered the king, "Do not think that the words this soul told us are lies.

For this soul said, 'You do not have the power to fight against Elias the Christian, because his God fights for him.' I believe the word is true, because I once heard of some ancient magicians, Egyptians, two brothers, one named Jannes
and the other Jambres, who set themselves against a man named Moses
and could not prevail against him,
because his God fought for him.
So now we too, O king, have been led astray in our folly; for whoever has God fighting for him, no one has power over him.
But I do not want to grieve you, O king. I will test Elias the Christian three times; if I cannot prevail against him, then truly no one has power over him."
The king went into the cell where the saint was shut in and found the seal he had set on it intact, just as it had been.
The king was saying, "Perhaps you will find that he has already died from the torture I put him to."
When he opened the door to go in, he smelled a great fragrance in the room. He looked and saw Saint Elias standing and praying, with great glory surrounding him.
When the king saw this, he was amazed; but the devils were leading his heart astray,
and he ordered the holy Elias to be brought out. The magician said
to the king, "Let us take this Christian
up the mountain outside, away from these crowds, and we will test each other today."
So the king went up the mountain with the magician and the saint.
The king said to him, "O Elias, I have brought you up this mountain to test you today." The saint said to him, "I do not know what magic is; but the power of Jesus my God is invincible."
The king turned to the magician and said to him, "Whatever you mean to do, do it quickly."
The magician stood and made his invocations, and the mountain split in two.
Two great and very fierce dragons came up. But Saint Elias did not look at them at all; he stood praying to God.
When the dragons saw the holy Elias praying, they stopped short
and stood still in fear, hiding themselves from him. When the magician saw this, he was utterly astonished. He labored at invoking the dragons, but they would not stir from their place.
The magician, wanting to please the king, said, "O Elias, do you think that you have held back the dragons
and kept them from coming near you because my art has run out? Behold, I tell you, I will do you harm."
After that he invoked the dragons and split them down the middle. He took the dragons' gall, their fat [?] and their liver, along with a dead raven and a wild [?], and mixed them together.
He put them in a new cup and invoked over them the names of demons,
so that the abyss split open and the devil came up, and the whole mountain was filled with demons in apparitions.
When the king saw this, he rejoiced greatly.

He took hold of the magician's head and kissed it, saying, "Truly I know that you are able to undo the magic of the Christians." The magician mixed the foul things together, put them into the cup and handed it to the righteous man. When he took it, he said, "I had no wish to drink these foul things.

But it is no concern of mine, for it is written in the Scripture: 'Even if they drink a deadly drug, it will not harm them.'" Then the holy Elias looked up to heaven and prayed thus: "Hear me, my Lord Jesus Christ, who hear everyone who cries out to you, who heard Abraham when he was a stranger,
who saved Isaac from the hands of the Philistines,
who saved Jacob from the hands of Esau, who saved Joseph from the hand of Potiphar's wife,
who saved Moses from the hands of Pharaoh
and from the hands of Jannes and Jambres:
I too, your servant Elias, beseech you to save me from these apparitions. Do not let them prevail over me, so that the enemy may not boast over me.
For I have heard in the holy Scripture: 'If God fights for us, who will be against us?' And again Elisha says, 'Those who fight for us are more than those against us.'
Now then, my Lord Jesus Christ, who saved Elisha from the hand of the king of Syria, save me too from the hands of these demons." And it came to pass
that when the blessed Elias had finished praying, behold, Michael the archangel came to him. He scourged all the demons and drove them off the mountain,
and the devil too turned into a flame of fire and flew away. The king did not see the angel, but only the holy Elias.
When Saint Elias saw the angel standing beside him, he rejoiced greatly. He signed himself in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit
and drank the cup full of foul things, and no harm came to him at all.
Instead his face flushed like that of a man drunk with wine.
When Publianus saw that no harm had come to Saint Elias,
he lifted up his hands and cried out, "Truly there is no god in heaven or on earth like Jesus Christ, who is mighty, the God of Saint Elias!"
The magician answered, "There is one more thing in which I will test you.
If no harm comes to you in it, then truly your God is the true one."
At once the magician made his invocations, and a great rock of fire rose up on the mountain before them.
He said to the righteous man, "If you trust your God with all your heart, that Jesus is a mighty God, then come and go into this rock of fire.
If no harm comes to you, I too will believe in your God."
Saint Elias lifted his eyes to heaven and prayed, saying, "I entreat you, Jesus, with whom nothing is impossible.
I entreat you, Jesus, hope of those who trust in you. I entreat you, Jesus, boast of the righteous, crown of the martyrs. You are the one who said in the holy Scriptures, 'Fire shall not harm you.'
And again you said, 'Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.' So I believe that you have power in all things.

You who saved the three saints from the burning furnace, save me too, so that your glory may be revealed before this magician and Publianus the senator." At once clouds of dew came out of heaven and covered the saint's body like a garment.
He signed himself and went into the fire,
and he spent two hours in the midst of the fire, praying. After that he came out of the fire.
No harm at all had come to him, nor was there even the smell of fire on his clothes.
The magician and the senator went up to him and greeted him, saying, "Truly your God Jesus is a true God,
and nothing is impossible for him. We beg you, O holy Elias, to entreat your God to grant us your crown of Christianity."

Saint Elias rejoiced greatly. He spread out his hands and prayed, saying, "I entreat you, my Lord Jesus Christ, the forgiving God: forgive Theocletus the magician and Publianus the senator. You said, 'I do not desire the death of the sinner so much as that he should turn back and repent.'
And again you said, 'I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.'
Now then, I entreat you to let this rock of fire be turned into springs of water, so that I may baptize those you have chosen in your holy name
and they may receive the seal of life. You said to your disciples, 'Go out into the whole world and baptize all the nations in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.'"
And at that very hour
the rock of fire was changed
and became a spring of water, its waters surging.
Then Saint Elias baptized Theocletus the magician and Publianus the senator,
and sealed them in the name of the Father and the Son
and the Holy Spirit, for the forgiveness of their sins.
When the king saw this, he was furious that the magician and the senator had believed in the Lord Jesus, and he came down the mountain with them.
He ordered the heads of the magician and the senator to be cut off together.
Publianus the senator had three friends, who came to visit him while he was in chains.

They said to him, "What is this that has happened to you, our friend? Has the king seized you over money you have not paid? If so, we will give you whatever the king has seized you for." He said to them, "If you are willing to listen to me—I, your friend, am the one telling you—do it.

I ask nothing of you except that you confess the God of Saint Elias, so that you may receive the imperishable crown forever." At once they cried out, "We are ready to die for his holy name!" And they all cried out to the king, "We are Christians!" Present there were Publius the senator, his three friends, his army of soldiers, his household servants, and Theocletus the magician as well. The king ordered pits to be dug and filled with fire, and the saints thrown into them,

and he burned them all in a single day. This is how Publius the senator, Theocletus the magician and all who were with them, nine hundred and seventy-four in number, completed their martyrdom on the twentieth [?] of Meshir; and they went up to heaven in glory.
After this they brought the holy Elias before the tribunal.
The king said to him, "Elias, do you think that because you have killed my magician I will be afraid of you and let you go?
By the might of my kingship,
I will torture you cruelly until I see whether Jesus can save you from my hands."
But Saint Elias kept completely silent,
and only gazed up to heaven.
The king ordered them to drive
two red-hot awls into his ears and two more into his eyes,
and after that to cut out his tongue,
so that his brain was burned. After that he ordered him laid on an iron bed
and boiling lead poured into his mouth.
But the holy Elias endured these tortures in [?]
…courage.
After this he had them flay the skin of his head and torture him.

And the holy one rose up from under yet another torture. After this he ordered them to dig a pit down into the ground, the size of his length and his breadth, and had them lower the holy one down into it. After this he had them light a fire under a cauldron full of lead until it became like water, and they turned the windlass and poured it down over his body until it came up to his neck. At once Michael the archangel stood over him and would not let the fire or the molten lead touch him at all; instead it was like cold water upon him.
When the king saw that he paid him no heed, he grew very angry.
The king rose, took his own knife, and with his own hand pierced the righteous man's heart, and his bowels fell down onto the ground.
At once, behold, a cloud of light overshadowed him, and the angel of the Lord took his bowels and put them back inside him before his eyes,
and he anointed his whole body, and he became as though they had never touched him at all.
When the king saw that he could not prevail over him,

he said, "I know what I will do: I will send him to Eutychodorus. Perhaps he has a magician with him who is very powerful." He rose there from the tribunal and ordered them to shut him in until he had written his report.
And he took a sheet of papyrus and wrote on it as follows: "I, Liberianus, king of Kounthia, write to Eutychodorus, king of the Medes: greetings.
Since the race of the Christians has risen in revolt with works of magic deserving of death,
behold, I have sent you one of them, whose name is Elias, so that you may put him to death."
Then he ordered them to bring out the holy Elias and hand him over to two protectors. They embarked and set sail on the sea, and they bound Saint Elias and threw him down into the hold of the ship.
When they had set out [?], Michael came down from heaven with a cloud of light. He went down into the hold of the ship, set Saint Elias free, and placed him on the cloud of light,
and carried him up to heaven.
He saw all the saints and greeted them, and they rejoiced over him. He carried him up to the third heaven,
and also into paradise, with the tree of life in its midst.
Again he brought him into the land of the inheritance.
He saw it: its soil was white like refined silver, and it bore countless fruits, exceedingly good.
Again they brought him to the city of Christ,
and twelve walls surrounded that city.
Again they showed him a great house like a royal palace, built within the wall, about fifteen stadia in breadth, built entirely of gold and pearls, and about a hundred cubits in height.
Its gates were built of precious stones and shone more brightly than the sun.

Michael said to him, "Saint Elias, this house built of gold and pearls is yours." When the holy Elias heard these words, he rejoiced greatly. And as he was walking in the city, behold, the Lord Jesus came out of heaven before him.
He said to him, "Be strong, O Elias, my beloved. Your contest has drawn near to you. Behold, you have seen how many good things I have prepared for those who will believe in me with all their heart.

I am Jesus, the joy of all the ages. Behold, I too rejoice with you today. As for you, my beloved, when they bring you to Media, Eutychodorus king of Media will put you to death, for it is through him that you will complete your contest."
Saint Elias answered and said to the Savior, "My Lord, I do not want to enter into the midst of the godless heathen, lest they scatter my bones and wipe out my memory from the earth."

The Savior said to him, "Truly I say to you, O my chosen Elias, just as the dew of heaven spreads over the whole earth, so will my name be glorified through you, because of the mighty works that will take place through your body.
And because you have asked me that your body be taken away from the heathen, I will set your heart at rest and fulfill your request.
After some days I will reveal your memory in a vision to righteous men who live in Egypt, and I will have them come for your body and carry it up to Egypt and lay it there.
And in the place where your body will be laid, I will have them lay the bodies of other righteous men,
two of them, there with you.
And the place where your body will be laid will become a temple for me forever.
And whoever comes into your shrine and asks me for any request in faith, in your name, I will grant it to him.
And anyone suffering from any sickness who comes into your shrine and entreats you in my name, I will grant them healing [?], and I will make your
name renowned everywhere, and I will cause great mighty works and wonders to take place in your resting place."
When the Lord Jesus had said these things, he went up to heaven in glory.
And at once the ship put in at the harbor of Media, the metropolis of the Medes,
and the protectors gave the letters to King Eutychodorus.
The second martyrdom of Saint Elias, which he underwent under Liberianus, king of Kounthia. In peace. Amen.

Now when they had delivered the report about Saint Elias to Eutychodorus, king of Media, he read everything that had been written to him and had him shut in until the next day, so that he could give him a hearing. He wrote letters in reply and sent them off
so that they might go back to their king, to their own country. The next day the king sat on the tribunal and had them bring the holy Elias to him.

The king said to him, "Elias, there are these evil deeds which have been written to me, that you do them. Now then, sacrifice." The righteous man answered, "It is written in the holy Scriptures: 'You shall not worship things made by hands, for I am God, and there is no other
besides me.'" When the king heard this, he had him hung up in a linen tunic, and they shot arrows at him for three hours.
But the holy Elias sealed himself with the sign of the cross.
At once, behold, a cloud of light covered him, and not a single arrow touched him at all.
When the king saw this, he was greatly amazed and ordered them to take him down from the wood.

The king said to him, "Elias, I want you to tell me about this sign which you made on your forehead, so that you were saved from these arrows. For I say in my heart that what you did is a work of magic; otherwise you would not have been saved." Saint Elias said to him, "O king, do not think that what I did is a work of magic, far from it! This is the sign of the cross of my Lord Jesus Christ." The king said to him, "They hanged your Lord? What did they do to him?"

The righteous man said to him, "He went up on the cross and died for our sins." The king said to him, "So your god died too, like any man?" The righteous man said, "Not at all. He is immortal; he died, but he rose again, so that he might give us life." The king said to him, "Truly, the death by which your god Jesus died is the death by which I will kill you too."
Then he ordered them to make a cross and hang the holy one on it. When they had set the holy one on it, he rejoiced, because he had been found worthy of the likeness of the Lord.
And at once, behold, a dove of light settled on the right arm of the cross,
and another on the left arm, and they spread their wings over him and covered him, for he was naked.
And behold, a voice came to him: "O Elias, behold the likeness which I bore, I the Son of God; behold, you too have borne it.
For they hanged me on the cross and placed me between two thieves. Truly I say to you, my chosen Elias, there is nothing greater than the likeness which you have borne."
And when Jesus had finished speaking with him, there were thunders and lightnings, and a great fear
fell upon everyone around him.
And behold, the angels came, set the holy one free, and brought him down from the cross. They took the cross and sped away, leaving Saint Elias standing.

When the king saw these things, he was amazed. He rose from the tribunal that day and had him shut in until the next day. The next day, because the king was very angry, since the devil had filled his heart with every evil against him, he at once sat on the tribunal and ordered them to bring the holy one to him. The king said to him, "Elias, do you think that because you practiced arts of magic until you were saved from the cross, there are no more tortures left for you?" The king ordered them to break the joints of his hands and of his feet,
and he endured it.
And he had them beat his head with an iron hammer until his brain came out through his mouth and his nostrils.
When the king saw that he had not died from all the things he had done to him,
he had them bring him wild beasts, exceedingly fierce: a leopard and a wild boar.
He had Saint Elias thrown to them, thinking that they would tear him open at once.

When the beasts saw Saint Elias praying to God, they ran to him wagging their tails at him, and they bowed down and worshiped him. The king was greatly amazed and knew that he could not prevail over him. He passed sentence on him, that they should cut off his head and carry him to an island in the sea and leave him there. As they were about to lead Saint Elias out to cut off his head, he turned his face to the east and prayed thus: "I bless you, my Lord Jesus Christ, because I have been found worthy to come to this hour, to die for your holy name. I beseech you, my Lord, do not put me to shame as I come to you."
At once the sweet voice of the Lord came to him: "Truly I say to you, O my chosen Elias, the will of my Father has been fulfilled in your contest.
Behold, my heavens have been adorned with crowns before you. Victorious is he who has conquered; mighty is he who has prevailed."
When the holy Elias heard this, he sealed himself in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit
and stretched out his neck, and they took off his head at the ninth hour on the fifteenth of Paremhat.
The angels and all the saints came out before him and greeted him,
and they sang the hymn of Alleluia until they had brought him to the city of Christ.
When they had taken off his head, they took his body and laid it on an island in the middle of the sea,

until the day when God revealed him in a vision to two righteous monks in the land of Egypt, that they should go for his body, bring it to Egypt, and lay it in the place which the Lord had prepared for him. This is how he completed his martyrdom. He went up to heaven in glory and received the incorruptible crown. In peace. Amen.

All those who were martyred with Saint Elias received the crown of everlasting life. They number six thousand four hundred and thirty souls, and with Saint Elias they entered into life. May their holy blessing be with us. Amen.
And this is how the holy Elias completed his honored contest on the fifteenth of Paremhat, having fallen into the hands of three kings, who are these:
Herodianus, king of the Enetoi [?], and Saint Elias was a native of that country;
the second is Liberianus, king of Kounthia; the third is Eutychodorus, king of the Medes, through whom he was made perfect and went up to heaven in glory and honor.
May it come to pass that we too attain the good things of the kingdom of heaven, through the grace
and love for humankind of our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom be glory, with his good Father and the Holy Spirit, life-giving and consubstantial, now and always, forever and ever. Amen.
